subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 58-year-old woman with a documented sulfa allergy is started on a new loop diuretic for edema. Three days later she develops fever and a widespread pruritic rash. The pharmacist flags the medication review, noting that many commonly prescribed drugs contain a sulfonamide group that must be avoided in these patients.
question: Which of the following drugs contains a sulfonamide group and should be avoided in patients with sulfa allergy?
explanation_correct: Furosemide is a sulfa drug. The sulfa drug list (Scary Sulfa Pharm FACTS) includes sulfonamide antibiotics, sulfasalazine, probenecid, furosemide, acetazolamide, celecoxib, thiazides, and sulfonylureas — all of which may trigger reactions in sulfa-allergic patients.

explanation_incorrect.B: Metformin is a biguanide antihyperglycemic and is not a sulfonamide-containing drug.
explanation_incorrect.C: Atenolol is a beta-blocker and does not carry a sulfonamide group.
explanation_incorrect.D: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor unrelated to the sulfa drug list.
explanation_incorrect.E: Amoxicillin is a penicillin-class antibiotic; penicillins cause their own hypersensitivity reactions but are not sulfa drugs.

educationalObjective: Sulfa drugs include sulfonamide antibiotics, sulfasalazine, probenecid, furosemide, acetazolamide, celecoxib, thiazides, and sulfonylureas.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 44-year-old woman with a history of sulfa allergy is inadvertently given a sulfonamide antibiotic for a urinary tract infection. She develops fever, generalized urticaria, and a painful rash with mucosal blistering and skin sloughing. Her physician is counseling her on the range of reactions her sulfa allergy may produce in the future.
question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized manifestation of sulfa allergy?
explanation_correct: Sulfa-allergic patients may develop fever, urinary tract infection, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, acute interstitial nephritis, urticaria, and photosensitivity. Hypokalemia is not a manifestation of sulfa allergy — it is an adverse effect of some diuretics and other drugs, not an allergic reaction to sulfonamides.

explanation_incorrect.A: Stevens-Johnson syndrome is a classic severe cutaneous reaction seen with sulfa drugs.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hemolytic anemia is a listed hematologic reaction to sulfonamides in sulfa-allergic patients.
explanation_incorrect.C: Acute interstitial nephritis is among the renal manifestations of sulfa drug reactions.
explanation_incorrect.E: Photosensitivity is a well-known skin manifestation of sulfa drug reactions.

educationalObjective: Sulfa allergy manifests as fever, SJS, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, interstitial nephritis, urticaria, UTI, and photosensitivity — not hypokalemia.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 62-year-old woman with osteoarthritis and a documented sulfa allergy asks for a medication review before her pharmacy fills a new anti-inflammatory prescription for joint pain. The physician needs to identify which of her proposed medications carries sulfonamide-related risk.
question: Which of the following medications should be avoided in this patient?
explanation_correct: Celecoxib is a COX-2 inhibitor that contains a sulfonamide group and is part of the sulfa drug list (Scary Sulfa Pharm FACTS). In a sulfa-allergic patient it may trigger fever, SJS, hemolytic anemia, interstitial nephritis, urticaria, or photosensitivity.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ibuprofen is a nonselective NSAID without a sulfonamide group and is not on the sulfa drug list.
explanation_incorrect.C: Colchicine treats gout by inhibiting microtubule polymerization and is not a sulfa drug.
explanation_incorrect.D: Etanercept is a TNF inhibitor; biologics are not sulfonamide-containing agents.
explanation_incorrect.E: Allopurinol reduces uric acid formation and causes rash and hypersensitivity of its own, but it is not a sulfa drug.

educationalObjective: Celecoxib contains a sulfonamide group and should be avoided in sulfa allergy.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 70-year-old man with heart failure, gout, glaucoma, a sulfa allergy, and chronic kidney disease has a medication list that includes several agents drawn from different drug classes. During a medication reconciliation, the physician asks which agent can be safely continued despite the documented sulfa allergy.
question: Which of the following medications can most likely be continued safely in this patient?
explanation_correct: Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker and is not a sulfa drug, so it can be continued in a sulfa-allergic patient. The other options are all on the sulfa drug list: sulfasalazine, probenecid, acetazolamide, and thiazide diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide may all trigger allergic reactions in these patients.

explanation_incorrect.A: Sulfasalazine is, by name and classification, a sulfonamide drug and should be avoided in sulfa allergy.
explanation_incorrect.B: Probenecid is a uricosuric that contains a sulfonamide group and is on the sulfa drug list.
explanation_incorrect.C: Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that is a classic sulfa drug.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic with a sulfonamide moiety and may provoke sulfa-allergic reactions.

educationalObjective: Amlodipine (a dihydropyridine CCB) is not a sulfa drug, unlike sulfasalazine, probenecid, acetazolamide, and thiazides.
